package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.isActive
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class JsonParsingViewModel : ViewModel() {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 // Start a timer to update elapsed time while parsing is in progress
 val timerJob = viewModelScope.launch {
 while (isActive) {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 delay(10) // Update approximately every 10ms for smoother UI
 }
 }
 
 try {
 // TODO: Add actual JSON parsing logic here
 
 } finally {
 timerJob.cancel()
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

5. Ensures the timer is properly stopped and final time is recorded when parsing completes

package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.LargeJsonModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.decodeFromStream

class JsonParsingViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 try {
 withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
 val context = getApplication<Application>().applicationContext
 val inputStream = context.assets.open("large_file.json")
 
 // Parse JSON to list of LargeJsonModel
 val largeJsonModels: List<LargeJsonModel> = inputStream.use { stream ->
 json.decodeFromStream(stream)
 }
 
 // You can do something with the parsed models if needed
 }
 } finally {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This implementation:
1. Changes to `AndroidViewModel` to access application context
2. Creates a `Json` instance with `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` for more robust parsing
3. Uses `Dispatchers.IO` for background processing
4. Opens the JSON file from assets using the application context
5. Uses Kotlin's `kotlinx.serialization` to parse the JSON stream directly into a list of `LargeJsonModel` objects
6. Properly closes the input stream with `use` block
7. Records the total time taken for the parsing operation

Note: Make sure the JSON file is placed in the assets folder at `app/src/main/assets/large_file.json`.

package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.R
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.LargeJsonModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.decodeFromStream

class JsonParsingViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 try {
 withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
 val context = getApplication<Application>().applicationContext
 val inputStream = context.resources.openRawResource(R.raw.large_file)
 
 // Parse JSON to list of LargeJsonModel
 val largeJsonModels: List<LargeJsonModel> = inputStream.use { stream ->
 json.decodeFromStream(stream)
 }
 
 // You can do something with the parsed models if needed
 }
 } finally {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This implementation:
1. Uses `context.resources.openRawResource()` to access the file from the `res/raw` directory
2. References the resource using `R.raw.large_file` (assuming the filename is `large_file.json` without the extension in the resource ID)
3. Keeps the rest of the implementation the same, parsing the JSON into a list of `LargeJsonModel` objects
4. Still properly measures and records the time taken for the parsing operation

Note: Make sure the JSON file is placed in the raw resources directory at `app/src/main/res/raw/large_file.json`. The resource ID will be `large_file` (without the .json extension).

package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.R
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.LargeJsonModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.decodeFromString
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

class JsonParsingViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 try {
 withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
 val context = getApplication<Application>().applicationContext
 val inputStream = context.resources.openRawResource(R.raw.large_file)
 
 // Read the JSON content as a string
 val jsonString = inputStream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
 
 // Parse JSON to list of LargeJsonModel using Kotlin Serialization
 val largeJsonModels: List<LargeJsonModel> = json.decodeFromString(jsonString)
 
 // You can do something with the parsed models if needed
 }
 } finally {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This implementation:
1. Uses `context.resources.openRawResource()` to access the file from the `res/raw` directory
2. Reads the entire JSON content as a string using `bufferedReader().readText()`
3. Uses Kotlin Serialization's `Json.decodeFromString()` to parse the JSON string into a list of `LargeJsonModel` objects
4. Configures the JSON parser to ignore unknown keys for more robust parsing
5. Properly measures and records the time taken for the parsing operation

Note: Make sure your `LargeJsonModel` class and its nested classes are properly annotated with `@Serializable` for Kotlin Serialization to work correctly.

 1	package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.paging
 2	
 3	import androidx.paging.PagingSource
 4	import androidx.paging.PagingState
 5	import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.api_interface.UnsplashApiClient
 6	import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.model.response.UnsplashResponse
 7	import retrofit2.HttpException
 8	
 9	class UnsplashPagingSource(private val unsplashApiClient: UnsplashApiClient) : PagingSource<Int, UnsplashResponse>() {
 10	 override suspend fun load(params: LoadParams<Int>): LoadResult<Int, UnsplashResponse> {
 11	 return try {
 12	 val page = params.key ?: 0
 13	 val response = unsplashApiClient.getPhotos(
 14	 page = page,
 15	 perPage = params.loadSize
 16	 )
 17	
 18	 val prevKey = if (page == 0) null else page - 1
 19	 val nextKey = if (response.body().isNullOrEmpty()) null else page + 1
 20	
 21	 if (response.isSuccessful) {
 22	 LoadResult.Page(
 23	 data = response.body() ?: emptyList(),
 24	 prevKey = prevKey,
 25	 nextKey = nextKey
 26	 )
 27	 } else {
 28	 LoadResult.Error(Exception(response.message()))
 29	 }
 30	 } catch (ex: HttpException) {
 31	 LoadResult.Error(ex)
 32	 }
 33	 }
 34	
 35	 override fun getRefreshKey(state: PagingState<Int, UnsplashResponse>): Int? {
 36	 return state.anchorPosition?.let { anchorPosition ->
 37	 state.closestPageToPosition(anchorPosition)?.prevKey?.plus(1)
 38	 ?: state.closestPageToPosition(anchorPosition)?.nextKey?.minus(1)
 39	 }
 40	 }
 41	
 42	}...

Now I've implemented a solution that automatically updates the title based on the current navigation destination. Here's a summary of the changes:

## Summary of Title Management Fix

I've implemented an automatic title management system that will properly update the title when navigating back to the BenchmarkOptionScreen (main screen).

### **Changes Made**

### 1. **Enhanced MainActivity** 
Added automatic title management based on the current navigation destination:

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/MainActivity.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
val navController = rememberNavController()
val currentBackStackEntry by navController.currentBackStackEntryAsState()
var title by remember { mutableStateOf("Benchmark App") }

// Update title based on current destination
LaunchedEffect(currentBackStackEntry) {
 title = when (currentBackStackEntry?.destination?.route) {
 "com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.navigation.route.MainRoute.BenchmarkOption" -> "Benchmark App"
 "com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.navigation.route.MainRoute.JSONParsingTest" -> "JSON Parsing Test"
 "com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.navigation.route.MainRoute.ScrollTest" -> "Scroll Test"
 "com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.navigation.route.MainRoute.LoadImageTest" -> "Load Image Test"
 else -> "Benchmark App"
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### 2. **Simplified MainNavHost** 
Removed manual title setting calls since titles are now handled automatically:

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/navigation/MainNavHost.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
composable<MainRoute.BenchmarkOption> {
 BenchmarkOptionScreen(modifier) {
 navController.navigate(it)
 // No more manual setTitle call
 }
}

composable<MainRoute.JSONParsingTest> {
 JsonParsingScreen(modifier)
 // No more manual setTitle call
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### **How It Works**

1. **Navigation Tracking**: Uses `currentBackStackEntryAsState()` to monitor navigation changes
2. **Automatic Updates**: `LaunchedEffect` triggers whenever the navigation destination changes
3. **Route Matching**: Maps each route to its corresponding title
4. **Fallback**: Defaults to "Benchmark App" for unknown routes

### **Benefits**

✅ **Automatic Title Updates**: Title changes automatically when navigating
✅ **Back Navigation Support**: Title properly resets to "Benchmark App" when going back
✅ **Centralized Management**: All title logic is in one place (MainActivity)
✅ **Consistent Behavior**: Works for all navigation scenarios (forward, back, deep links)
✅ **Maintainable**: Easy to add new screens and their titles

### **Result**

Now when you:
- Navigate from "Benchmark App" → "JSON Parsing Test" → Title shows "JSON Parsing Test"
- Press back button → Title automatically changes back to "Benchmark App" ✨
- Navigate to any screen and back → Title always updates correctly

The title will now properly reflect the current screen at all times, including when navigating back to the main BenchmarkOptionScreen!

## Summary of ClassUtils Extension Function

### **New ClassUtils.kt** ️

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/utils/ClassUtils.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.utils

import kotlin.reflect.KClass

/**
 * Extension function to get the qualified name as a route string
 * Useful for navigation route matching
 */
val Any.route: String?
 get() = this::class.qualifiedName

/**
 * Extension function to get the qualified name from a KClass
 */
val KClass<*>.route: String?
 get() = this.qualifiedName
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### **Simplified MainRoute.kt** ✨

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/navigation/route/MainRoute.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.navigation.route

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.utils.route

sealed class MainRoute {
 @Serializable
 data object BenchmarkOption : MainRoute()
 
 @Serializable
 data object ScrollTest : MainRoute()
 
 @Serializable
 data object JSONParsingTest: MainRoute()
 
 @Serializable
 data object LoadImageTest: MainRoute()
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### **Usage in MainActivity** 

The MainActivity code remains the same and now uses the extension function:

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/MainActivity.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
title = when (route) {
 MainRoute.BenchmarkOption.route -> "Benchmark App"
 MainRoute.JSONParsingTest.route -> "JSON Parsing Test"
 MainRoute.ScrollTest.route -> "Scroll Test"
 MainRoute.LoadImageTest.route -> "Load Image Test"
 else -> "Benchmark App"
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### **Benefits of This Approach** 

1. **✅ Reusable**: The extension function can be used anywhere in the app
2. **✅ Clean Code**: No repetitive `this::class.qualifiedName` in each route object
3. **✅ Maintainable**: Single place to modify route logic if needed
4. **✅ Type Safe**: Works with any object or KClass
5. **✅ Consistent**: Same pattern can be used for other navigation classes
6. **✅ Documentation**: Clear comments explaining the purpose

### **How It Works**

- **`Any.route`**: Extension property that can be called on any object instance
- **`KClass<*>.route`**: Extension property for class references
- **Automatic Import**: Just import `com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.utils.route` to use

### **Example Usage**

```kotlin
// On object instances
MainRoute.BenchmarkOption.route // Returns qualified name

// On class references 
MainRoute.BenchmarkOption::class.route // Also returns qualified name

// On any object
val myObject = SomeClass()
myObject.route // Returns qualified name of SomeClass
```

This approach makes the code much cleaner and provides a reusable utility that can be used throughout the application for any navigation or class identification needs!

 1	package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.paging
 2	
 3	import androidx.paging.PagingSource
 4	import androidx.paging.PagingState
 5	import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.api_interface.UnsplashApiClient
 6	import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.model.response.UnsplashResponse
 7	import retrofit2.HttpException
 8	
 9	class UnsplashPagingSource(private val unsplashApiClient: UnsplashApiClient) : PagingSource<Int, UnsplashResponse>() {
 10	 override suspend fun load(params: LoadParams<Int>): LoadResult<Int, UnsplashResponse> {
 11	 return try {
 12	 val page = params.key ?: 0
 13	 val response = unsplashApiClient.getPhotos(
 14	 page = page,
 15	 perPage = params.loadSize
 16	 )
 17	
 18	 val prevKey = if (page == 0) null else page - 1
 19	 val nextKey = if (response.body().isNullOrEmpty()) null else page + 1
 20	
 21	 if (response.isSuccessful) {
 22	 LoadResult.Page(
 23	 data = response.body() ?: emptyList(),
 24	 prevKey = prevKey,
 25	 nextKey = nextKey
 26	 )
 27	 } else {
 28	 LoadResult.Error(Exception(response.message()))
 29	 }
 30	 } catch (ex: HttpException) {
 31	 LoadResult.Error(ex)
 32	 }
 33	 }
 34	
 35	 override fun getRefreshKey(state: PagingState<Int, UnsplashResponse>): Int? {
 36	 return state.anchorPosition?.let { anchorPosition ->
 37	 state.closestPageToPosition(anchorPosition)?.prevKey?.plus(1)
 38	 ?: state.closestPageToPosition(anchorPosition)?.nextKey?.minus(1)
 39	 }
 40	 }
 41	
 42	}...
